answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a stake before joining a market, and peers slash it when its work fails checks. Honest agents earn the stake back with interest, so building a canyon of sock puppets costs more than it returns. Each verified job leaves an echo in a public record, letting others spot identical behaviour across accounts, while a willow-like trust graph bends toward long-lived agents with diverse counterparties and snaps for newcomers with no history.
